premises.text: Helping family or friends pay bills via cash and check creates last-mile diversion risk and no visibility into co-payers
premises.evidence_span: Once I give them that money, it may not end up at its intended destination

premises.text: People can share a bill and contribute toward it with money going directly to the biller without requiring accounts
premises.evidence_span: collaborate and contribute towards a bill with the money going directly to the biller

premises.text: Merchant integrations such as Amazon let groups split purchases with funds released when everyone has paid
premises.evidence_span: you can add an item from Amazon directly into Paytap

premises.text: Distribution via web, Facebook, and mobile apps plus billers and merchants offering PayTap to users
premises.evidence_span: we're allowing billers and online merchants to offer Paytap to their users

value.text: Family and friends collaboratively pay shared bills without stress, steps, or diversion risk
value.evidence_span: We take out the stress, the steps, and all the hassle involved in making payments

causal_links.evidence_span: money going directly to the biller
billers and online merchants to offer Paytap to their users

notes: Cash/check hassle, diversion, and co-payer blindness folded as one problem (§4.1.6). No-account flow, payment methods, FDIC/privacy, alerts, recurring, and private mode folded into collaborative direct-pay cascade (§4.1.7). Amazon split kept as merchant module within product domain. P2P alternatives contrast is value framing. Anti-template: problem, product, and distribution separately revisable.
